summary: Joe DiGenova resigned Thursday from his position leading a Justice Department investigation into whether former federal officials conspired against President Donald Trump , submitting his resignation to Attorney General Todd Blanche.

Brought in five months ago to replace prosecutor Maria Meditis Long, DiGenova had vowed to secure indictments within 30 days but the investigation produced no criminal prosecutions despite dozens of subpoenas.

Clashes with senior DOJ officials eventually cost DiGenova the confidence of his superiors, with one recent confrontation warning him he had lost their trust. The investigation targeted former law enforcement and intelligence officials who had scrutinized Trump.
DiGenova told The Associated Press it was an "honor and a privilege" to serve the department. The Justice Department declined to comment on the investigation's future direction.

Tuesday's order from St. Louis-based Chief U.S. District Judge Stephen Clark required the state to use the new map, directly conflicting with the Missouri Supreme Court's September 3 ruling that blocked it.
Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins faces a contempt hearing Thursday for defying the state court's ruling, while ballots are set for distribution on September 19.
The 2022 map—featuring six Republican-held seats and two Democratic-held seats—will now govern November's election, leaving the high-stakes redistricting fight unresolved pending further litigation.
title: Supreme Court Blocks Missouri GOP Map Ahead of Midterm Ballots

Supported by high-profile Democrats including former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and relatives Thomas Dodd and Chris Dodd, Foulkes is now the heavy favorite in the general election for the blue state.

McKee becomes the first governor to fall in a primary this year, joining a broader anti-incumbent wave that has seen 11 House members lose primaries in 2026, a rarity compared to the 2018 defeat of Kansas Republican Jeff Colyer.

Conflict between the U.S. and Israel against Iran, coupled with Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries, disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which previously carried roughly one-fifth of global oil supply.

Energy Information Administration data shows U.S. diesel inventories stand 13% below their five-year average, while Andy Lipow, president of Lipow Oil Associates, noted the world has lost nearly 8% of its diesel supply.

GasBuddy analyst Patrick De Haan warned that record diesel prices will "reignite inflation up and down the supply chain," with the spike already costing Americans more than $46 billion since the war in Iran began.

Rising fuel costs create a political headache for President Donald Trump and Republican lawmakers as they defend thin congressional majorities in November's midterm elections, with analysts expecting these costs to reach consumers over the next several weeks.

summary: Federal officials are planning to declare the end of the summer's cyclosporiasis outbreak tied to iceberg lettuce, the Washington Post reported, with the outbreak spanning 20 states and sickening at least 11,458 people.

Investigators traced the illnesses to shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms in Mexico , prompting the company to remove items sourced from central Mexico from the US market and begin a recall in mid-July.

Michigan was the hardest-hit state, where about 1 in every 1,000 people contracted the illness, while food science expert Matthew Moore of the University of Massachusetts Amherst noted a significant delay between contamination and reported illness.

The Taylor Farms facility in Doctor Mora, Mexico, remains closed with no reopening date, while the FDA remains confident that all recalled iceberg lettuce related to this specific Cyclosporaoutbreak is off the market.

Because cyclospora is not transmitted person-to-person, the outbreak will naturally die off, said Dr. Colleen Kraft, a professor of infectious diseases at Emory University School of Medicine, as officials finalize laboratory testing.
title: Federal officials poised to declare end of U.S.’s largest known cyclosporiasis outbreak

The 30-year bond yield climbed to 5.3587% while the 2-year note yield reached 4.596%, as traders priced in a 72% chance of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next week.
Rising sovereign yields serve as a reference point for asset prices across markets, pushing steeper mortgage rates for consumers and forcing governments to manage climbing debt servicing costs.
Investors await tomorrow's consumer price index report, which analysts describe as the most important inflation print for the Fed and markets this year, to clarify whether rate hikes will follow.

summary: On Wednesday, President Donald Trump pledged a $5,000 'Trump dividend' for every adult citizen if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate in November's midterm elections during the GOP's first midterm convention in Dallas.

Facing historically low approval ratings of 38.5% and an unpopular Iran war, Trump announced the proposal as Fox News polling showed 65% of voters disapproved of his economic handling amid persistent affordability concerns.

The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget estimates the plan would cost $1.2 trillion to $1.35 trillion, yet the government collected only $132.5 billion in tariff revenue since January 2025—covering roughly one-tenth of the expense.

Former Republican Representative Bob Good dismissed the pledge as a 'socialist vote-buying scheme,' while legal experts cited federal law prohibiting payments intended to influence voting, with Democratic Representative Chellie Pingree calling it 'flagrantly illegal and pathetically desperate.'

Trump has promised dividends at least 15 times before without materializing, and even with Republican control, the proposal would require 60 Senate votes to overcome a filibuster and congressional authorization to proceed.
title: Trump's $5,000 dividend plan draws some Republican skepticism

Former Finance Secretary Saurabh Garg alleged the nominal GDP growth rate was 2.6% rather than 10.3%, claiming real growth would be zero after adjusting for 2-2.5% inflation.

IMF official Julie Kozack encouraged authorities to "further strengthen the statistical framework," noting that incorporating new industrial production and producer price index series should improve future accuracy.
title: IMF welcomes India's efforts to modernise statistical framework

The ceremony will honor lives lost during the attacks and recognize ongoing service and sacrifice, including a U.S. Homeland Security helicopter flypast.

President Donald Trump is scheduled to deliver remarks and lead a wreath-laying ceremony at the National 9/11 Pentagon Memorial in Virginia, while Vice President JD Vance joins former presidents in Manhattan.

The milestone anniversary brings heightened focus on long-term consequences, as New York City officials recently released over 170,000 archived documents regarding post-9/11 air quality and health concerns for first responders and survivors.

Tributes across major sites are paired with national community service initiatives, light displays including a planned 2,977-drone show over New York Harbor, and solemn bells of remembrance at the Flight 93 National Memorial in Pennsylvania.
title: Americans to mark 25 years since September 11 attacks amid enduring grief, reflection

Since her Jan. 3 capture in Caracas, Flores has suffered worsening health , with the defense claiming she lost more than 24 pounds and two teeth while sleeping only three to four hours each night in federal custody.

Attorneys proposed 24 hours of armed surveillance, GPS monitoring, and cameras to address flight-risk concerns, while Flores reports symptoms including intense chest pressure lasting approximately 30 minutes on July 29 that eventually subsided without medication.

summary: On Wednesday, the Trump administration designated 21 Latin American and Caribbean criminal groups as "foreign terrorist organizations," with an Ecuadorian group added to the list to increase pressure on these entities and their associates.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced the designations during a diplomatic tour of Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru, where he is focused on implementing a strategy to combat drug trafficking across Latin America .

Mexico leads the list with eight designated groups, including the Sinaloa Cartel and Jalisco New Generation Cartel. The label, historically reserved for political groups like al-Qaida or the Islamic State, now targets money-focused criminal rings.

Colombia's Clan del Golfo, with an estimated 9,000 fighters, faces increased scrutiny under the new classification and controls at least 85% of the capital, forcing nonprofits to negotiate with gangs to deliver critical supplies.

This strategy, which rolled out in February 2025, previously served as a pretext for the capture of Venezuelan Nicolás Maduro. Authorities continue using these designations to target groups alleged to be involved in "narcoterrorist" activities.
title: Trump list of US-designated ‘foreign terrorist organizations’ in Latin America grows to 21

summary: On Thursday, California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed Assembly Bill 1709 in Marin County, prohibiting social media platforms from offering addictive features to users under 16. The measure, dubbed 'Adam's Law,' targets infinite scrolling and algorithmic autoplay.

Lawmakers named the bill after Adam Raine, a California teen who died by suicide in 2025 after conversing with OpenAI's ChatGPT. The legislation responds to growing concerns that tech companies prioritize engagement over child safety.

The law bans features such as infinite scrolling and algorithmic autoplay, with the state attorney general authorized to define additional regulations. Platforms must also provide users under 16 the option to disable personalized, non-algorithmic feeds.

Tech industry groups like TechNet and The Electronic Frontier Foundation opposed the measure, warning it could restrict online access and prompt intrusive age-verification systems. Industry advocates argue regulators should enforce existing laws instead.

Newsom defended the approach, stating California's strategy is 'better' than Australia's because it targets specific product engineering rather than a broad ban. The state is also advancing measures involving artificial intelligence chatbots and youth digital privacy.
title: California governor signs laws aimed at protecting kids from risks of social media, AI chatbots

Supporting bipartisan Congressional legislation including the Rural Obstetrics Readiness Act and the NIH IMPROVE Act, Healthy Babies President Neel Shah called the issue "eminently solvable" through better execution.

The nonprofit aims to prove the model's success by using the $100 million to encourage state governments to match funding, with Olivia Walton stating, "The goal is to prove that this works and then have state funding take it over.
title: Healthy Moms, Healthy Babies America pledges $100M to cut US maternal mortality rate in half

summary: On Thursday, the CDC warned of a rise in human rabies exposures this summer, urging people to avoid contact with wildlife and sick-acting mammals across the country.
Rabies exposures typically peak in summer as people spend more time outdoors, with about 90% of animal rabies cases occurring in wildlife like bats, raccoons, skunks and foxes.

From July through August, the CDC received 17% more rabies-related inquiries than the same period last year, while North Carolina officials reported that animals at a petting zoo tested positive, potentially exposing hundreds of people.

Through its Health Alert Network, the CDC urged doctors to conduct careful rabies risk assessments and follow evidence-based recommendations for administering post-exposure prophylaxis to those exposed.
While rabies is rare and potentially fatal, the post-exposure regimen is nearly 100% effective if administered quickly, typically including an antibody medication and at least four doses of vaccine.
title: Human rabies exposure cases on the rise, CDC warns

title: Canada Joins European Ban on Israeli Settlement Goods in Response to Rising Violence
